title: Austria Ground Motion
description: European Ground Motion Service (EGMS) Ortho Level 3 data for Austria, derived from Sentinel-1 C-band SAR interferometry (InSAR). The dataset provides gridded ground motion at 100 m resolution in ETRS89-LAEA (EPSG:3035) for the vertical (U) and east-west (E) components, for the periods 2016–2022 and 2016–2023. Each item contains mean velocity (mm/year), RMSE, seasonality and merge quality layers as Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs. The full displacement time series of each 100 m grid cell of the 2016–2023 release is available as point features via the linked OGC API - Features collections. Source: [EGMS](https://egms.land.copernicus.eu/).

title: Copernicus Global Land Surface Soil Moisture
description: The Copernicus Global Land Surface Soil Moisture product (CGLS_SSM) displays the relative water content of the top few centimetres soil, describing how wet or dry the soil is in its topmost layer, expressed in percent saturation. Input for the product are the Sentinel-1 C-band SAR backscatter values. Further information can be found [here] (https://land.copernicus.eu/global/products/ssm) and in Bauer-Marschallinger et al., 2018.

title: DestinE Climate Change Adaptation Digital Twin
description: The DestinE Climate Change Adaptation Digital Twin (Climate DT) delivers global climate projections and impact-sector information on multi-decadal timescales (1990–2050) at very high spatial resolutions (5–10 km). It integrates state-of-the-art Earth-system models, impact-sector applications, and observations into a unified framework. The Climate DT is the first operational system for global multi-decadal climate projections, running on EuroHPC supercomputing facilities using leading European climate models, including a new generation of global storm-resolving and eddy-rich models. Simulations cover the recent past (from 1990) through possible future climate evolutions to 2050. More information here: https://confluence.ecmwf.int/display/DDCZ/Climate+DT+Phase+1+data+catalogue

title: DestinE Climate Change Adaptation Digital Twin Volumetric Soil moisture
description: The Destination Earth Climate Change Adaptation Digital Twin (Climate DT) is an operational modeling system that delivers globally consistent, high-resolution climate and climate-impact data at spatial resolutions fine enough to capture many climate change effects and extreme weather events. This collection draws on Generation 2 data and covers the volumetric soil moisture (vsw). title: Drought Vulnerability
description: The map shows the average frequency of long-lasting droughts in Austria at a spatial resolution of 1km. The map can for example be used to calculate risk premiums for parametric insurance schemes. The MODIS derived drought vulnerability index is based on the occurrence of at least 3-month long vegetation anomalies of the months May to September and is derived from carefully filtered MODIS NDVI time series acquired between 2003 and 2018. The Institute of Geomatics at BOKU produces this indicator with a global coverage. Products derived using other date ranges and at improved spatial resolution (at 250m) are available on request from the Institute of Geomatics, University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, BOKU (Austria).

title: ERA5-Land hourly datacube
description: [ERA5-Land](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/reanalysis-era5-land) is a global reanalysis of land-surface conditions, produced by ECMWF for the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) by replaying the land component of the ERA5 climate reanalysis at higher resolution. It gives a consistent, gap-free reconstruction of past weather over land. This collection holds five of its variables, hourly from 1990 to a few days ago, on the native global 0.1° (about 9 km) regular lat/lon grid: 2 m air temperature (`t2m`), top-layer soil temperature (`stl1`), top-layer volumetric soil water (`swvl1`), snow depth (`sde`) and total precipitation (`tp`). Typical uses are climate, hydrology and agriculture analyses that need long, consistent time series. **Access.** The collection has no items. The data is one [Icechunk](https://icechunk.io) GeoZarr datacube, reached through the two collection assets, which hold the same data in two layouts: `/space` (map-optimized) and `/time` (time-series-optimized). Opening it needs the `icechunk` Python library (for example with xarray); plain Zarr clients cannot read it. Product details: [ERA5-Land data documentation](https://confluence.ecmwf.int/display/CKB/ERA5-Land%3A+data+documentation). **Maturity.** Hours before `era5land:consolidated_until` (exclusive) are final ERA5-Land (`expver=0001`). Later hours are preliminary ERA5T (`expver=0005`) and are replaced in place once ECMWF consolidates them. **Latest data.** The latest ingested hour is not tracked here: read the `ingested_until` attribute of the `/space` or `/time` group. **Precipitation.** `tp` is hourly de-accumulated: the value at time t covers the hour ending at t. **Sources.** Backfilled from the CDS `reanalysis-era5-land-timeseries` ARCO store, then kept current from the CDS API (`reanalysis-era5-land`). **Attribution.** Licensed CC-BY-4.0. Cite the dataset (see `sci:citation`) and state: "Generated using Copernicus Climate Change Service information <year>". Neither the European Commission nor ECMWF is responsible for any use that may be made of the Copernicus information or data it contains.

title: Sentinel-1 Alps WetSnow
description: Sentinel-1 based Wet Snow Maps in the EODC Data Catalogue are available for the full Alpine domain (50°N / 4°E – 43°N / 18°E) for the melting seasons (March – July) 2019 and 2021. The Wet Snow Map (WSM) provides binary information on the snow melt extent, based on Sentinel-1 C-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) repeat pass data, at the image acquisition time (given in UTC). At C-band, the typical one-way penetration depth of the radar signal into a dry seasonal snow pack is about 20 m, but reduces to only 3 cm for a wet snow pack with a liquid water content of 5% by volume (Mätzler, 1987). This means that for wet snow, the C-band radar signal is reflected and scattered at the surface and the uppermost centimetres of the snowpack. But for dry seasonal snow, a main contribution of the measured signal comes from the snow / ground interface, constraining a reliable discrimination of dry snow areas and snow free ground from Sentinel-1 SAR satellite data. The WSM generated with the change detection method of Nagler et al. (2016) indicates if there is any melt layer within the snowpack. Products are generated per Sentinel-1 track with a pixel spacing of 100 m x 100 m. Sentinel-1A and Sentinel-1B data from ascending (afternoon acquisitions) and descending (morning acquisitions) orbits are used for the WSM product generation. WSM products are generated every 6 days per Sentinel-1 track for the melting seasons 2019 and 2021. To avoid misclassifications in the valleys, e.g. due to agricultural activities, an a priori information on the snow-covered area per pixel is added. Information on the areal snow cover fraction per pixel is generated from daily optical satellite data of Sentinel-3 A&B SLSTR & OLCI with a pixel spacing of 200 m x 200 m. The fractional snow cover (FSC) per pixel is generated with a multi-spectral unmixing approach with locally adaptive end-member selection (Keuris et al., 2023). Earth observations by optical satellite data can be limited by clouds, while SAR satellite measurements are independent of cloud coverage or daylight. To fully exploit the Sentinel-1 SAR time series for the WSM generation, the snow cover fraction for cloud covered pixels in the optical satellite data is assimilated using a snowpack model driven by ERA5 reanalysis data of gridded temperature and precipitation fields. From the resulting map of the same date as the Sentinel-1 acquisition, pixels with at least 40% FSC are considered for the wet snow classification from Sentinel-1 data. The three categories 1) snow free pixels, 2) pixels with less than 40% FSC, and 3) pixels with dry snow are merged into one class in the WSM product. Water bodies, forested areas, and pixels affected by radar shadow, layover or foreshortening are masked in the WSM product. Water bodies are masked based on the maximum extent of permanent and seasonal water of the Copernicus Global Surface Water yearly classifications 2017 – 2021 (Pekel et al., 2016). The water layers with an original pixel spacing of about 30 m x 30 m are reprojected and aggregated to the grid of the WSM product, and considered as water if an aggregated pixel is covered by more than 30% water. Forests are masked based on the Copernicus Tree Cover Fraction product with an original pixel spacing of about 100 m x 100 m for the reference year 2019 (Buchhorn et al., 2020), based on optical satellite data acquired between 1 April 2017 and 31 March 2020. *Further information and links to access to satellite data and auxiliary layers used for the WSM generation:* Satellite input data are freely available after registration: - Copernicus Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-3 SLSTR & OLCI data: [Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem | Europe's eyes on Earth](https://dataspace.copernicus.eu/) Auxiliary layers are freely available and accessible via the following links: - Copernicus Global Surface Water: [Global Surface Water - Data Access (global-surface-water.appspot.com)](https://global-surface-water.appspot.com/download)) - Copernicus Tree Cover Fraction 2019: [Land Cover 2019 (raster 100 m), global, yearly – version 3 — Copernicus Land Monitoring Service](https://land.copernicus.eu/en/products/global-dynamic-land-cover/copernicus-global-land-service-land-cover-100m-collection-3-epoch-2019-globe) - ECMWF ERA5 data: [https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/) *References:* - Buchhorn, M., Bertels, L., Smets, B., De Roo, B., Lesiv, M., Tsendbazar, N. - E., Masiliunas, D., Li, L., 2020. Copernicus Global Land Service: Land Cover 100m: version 3 Globe 2015-2019: Algorithm Theoretical Basis Document; 2020. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.3606361 - Keuris, L., Hetzenecker, M., Nagler, T., Mölg, N., Schwaizer, G., 2023. An Adaptive Method for the Estimation of Snow-Covered Fraction with Error Propagation for Applications from Local to Global Scales. Remote Sensing 15, 1231. https://doi.org/10.3390/rs15051231 - Mätzler, C., 1987. Applications of the interaction of microwaves with the natural snow cover. Remote Sensing Reviews 2, 259–387. https://doi.org/10.1080/02757258709532086 - Nagler, T., Rott, H., Ripper, E., Bippus, G., Hetzenecker, M., 2016. Advancements for Snowmelt Monitoring by Means of Sentinel-1 SAR. Remote Sensing 8, 348. https://doi.org/10.3390/rs8040348 - Pekel, J.-F., Cottam, A., Gorelick, N., Belward, A.S., 2016. High-resolution mapping of global surface water and its long-term changes. Nature 540, 418–422. https://doi.org/10.1038/nature20584

title: SENTINEL1 Harmonic Parameters
description: The Harmonic model describes the typical seasonal Sentinel-1 backscatter variation on a 20 m pixel level. It was designed as a smoothed time-series approximation, removing short-term perturbations, such as speckle and transient events (like floods for instance). Hence, the model is suited to discern the seasonal changes brought about by varying water content, e.g., inundation or soil moisture, and progression of vegetation structure. The complete Sentinel-1 time-series dataset is challenging to analyse, primarily due to its sheer data volume of at the (global) scale of Petabytes. As a user-friendly alternative, this dataset provides a Harmonic (Fourier) series model that reduces the SAR backscatter seasonality to a relative small number of harmonic coefficient values. Seven coefficients computed using (harmonic) least squares regression, along with the standard deviation of residuals and number of observations, comprise the harmonic parametner set. The parameters are being operationally used to determine the expected SAR backscatter signal for any day of the year as part of the TU Wien's method contributing to GFM's ensemble flood monitoring effort (Bauer-Marschallinger et. al, 2022 https://www.mdpi.com/2072-4292/14/15/3673). The Global Harmonic Parameters (HPARs) were derived from the whole Sentinel-1 VV temporal stack for the period 2019-2020 by least squares regression with a harmonic model formulation, running three sinusoidal iterations (k=3). This dataset was generated by the Remote Sensing Group of the TU Wien Department of Geodesy and Geoinformation, within Framework Contract (No. 939866-IPR-2020) as part of the provision of an automated, global, satellite-based flood monitoring product for the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) managed by the European Commission. The Global Flood Monitoring (GFM) product is integrated within the user interface of the Global Flood Awareness System (GloFAS) of the CEMS.

title: Sentinel-5P Daily Aggregated Atmospheric Data for Austria
description: Daily mean atmospheric composition centered on Austria, derived from [Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI](https://sentinel.esa.int/web/sentinel/missions/sentinel-5p) Level-2 swath products. Data are regridded from native swath geometry onto a common 10 km grid and stored in Zarr format. Eight variables are included: carbon monoxide, ozone, methane, nitrogen dioxide, sulfur dioxide, formaldehyde, cloud fraction, and aerosol index, each as a daily mean with an observation count band. The grid extends beyond Austria's borders into neighboring parts of Italy, Germany, and the Balkans, providing spatial context for cross-border pollutant transport. Suited to regional air quality and atmospheric composition monitoring.

title: Vegetation-Change-Austria
description: This layer indicates vegetation change (persistence, increase, decrease, absence etc.) within three time periods (years). The layer is an RGB-colour multi-temporal representation of vegetation, where each colour represents one of three different time periods. All available Sentinel-2 images for three years (one for each colour) went into the analysis. For each year the vegetation observation was quantified (percentage of all yearly observations) using a standardized and fully automated semantic enrichment of EO images (https://color33.io), which identifies vegetation automatically based on spectral signatures. The RGB colour model is an additive colour model used to visualise the three different grayscale layers for each time period. It displays the changes from and within the three periods on the map within one layer using the different colour combinations. The interpretation of the colours can be drawn from the colour cube. The RGB colour palette and colour cube for the interpretation indicates change (increase and decrease) as well as persistence (white and very bright colours) or absence of vegetation (black/very dark). Changes in vegetation intensity and/or partly changed vegetation can be identified by the colour intensity. Service requests for other spatiotemporal extents can be made through the contact on the INTERFACE Website This layer focuses on vegetation / non-vegetation changes based on Sentinel-2 big EO data, which means at least one image every 5 days, and in higher latitudes and overlapping orbits even more. A specific service for calculating layers for custom analysis periods (e.g. years or seasons) or areas is available on request through the contact on the INTERFACE Website (https://interface.eodc.eu). Implementation by the Paris Lodron University Salzburg and Spatial Services GmbH
